findings_summary: Independent adversarial review of the review-package privacy builder and governance changes across four review rounds. One critical privacy fail-open (a tracked symlink embedded its target's CONTENT in the tar linkname field via readFileSync) and several medium/low correctness and metadata-disclosure defects were found, all fixed and re-verified; a final terminal review returned APPROVE with no blocking findings. The content boundary (restricted/untracked content never entering the archive) holds under every probe: tracked Promps/private.md, tracked symlink to a restricted file, tracked symlink to an untracked file, symlink chains, symlinks escaping the root, absolute targets, and backslash/over-long path forms.

findings.description: Tracked symlink archived with linkname = readFileSync(abs), which FOLLOWS the link and embedded the target file's content (restricted tracked, restricted untracked, or arbitrary untracked) into the tar linkname — a reproducible privacy fail-open.
ustar name handling silently truncated paths >100/255 bytes, so archive entries disagreed with inventory.json and MANIFEST.sha256.
git paths were backslash-normalized on Linux (where backslash is a legal filename character), causing misleading aborts and duplicate tar entries.
git() output was untrimmed, so inventory.head/branch/head_commit_time carried a trailing newline and the packaged SHA was unusable verbatim in a review record.

Validator treated the self-referential evidence_commit == code_head_reviewed shape as a warning only, HUMAN_APPROVAL did not require human_approval:true, and the shipped template failed its own validator.
restricted_untracked reported an untracked-only count, reading as 'nothing here' for a private root excluded because it is tracked.
The review-evidence validator was not invoked in CI, so the format rule was documentation-only.
A symlink linkname longer than 100 bytes was truncated while MANIFEST.sha256 hashed the full target, so the archive disagreed with its own manifest and the extracted link dangled.
An absolute inside-root symlink target was recorded verbatim, disclosing the local build layout.
A symlink chain (a -> b -> restricted) kept a dangling 'a -> b' after b was dropped.
The CLI allowlist normalized backslashes while classifyPaths did not; the two paths disagreed.
The CI review-evidence step validated nothing because the directory held only the non-matching template, so it could not catch a rotted template.
The archived inventory leaked the NAME of a restricted or untracked symlink target via package.symlink_excluded[].target, contradicting the module's 'counts only, never names' contract.
A tracked root file named inventory.json or MANIFEST.sha256 produced duplicate archive entries and made file_count disagree with the archive.
No unit test covered the --dir template validation behaviour.
The module header comment over-claimed that no restricted/private path name is ever emitted, while excluded_restricted_tracked legitimately lists tracked names.
A symlink to the bare restricted root (dirlink -> Promps) was labelled target_kind 'not-packaged' because the restricted globs were Promps/** and did not match the bare root.
An unrepresentable UNTRACKED path (e.g. a backslash filename) was emitted by name in package.excluded_unrepresentable, contradicting the header contract.
git()'s trim() stripped the leading space of the first `git status --porcelain` line, so tracked_modified_paths[0] was reported mangled (README.md -> EADME.md).
